thread.title: Alexandria Mobile Home Park to see new owners, hopeful to have water restored - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Alexandria Mobile Home Park to see new owners, hopeful to have water restored - NewsBreak

author: Gabriella Morando
title: Alexandria Mobile Home Park to see new owners, hopeful to have water restored - NewsBreak
text:
By Gabriella Morando ,
2 hours ago
ALEXANDRIA, Ind. — Amanda Davis has forgotten what it’s like to turn on her sink to wash her hands or scrub dishes with ease. It’s been 72 days since she was able to do just that.
It’s not just her sink. Her shower and laundry machines run dry. Her toilet has to be forcefully flushed with buckets of water.
She and others at the Alexandria Mobile Home Park have been without running water since August.
“Oh, I’m going to cry,” Davis said. “I’m ready. I’m ready for it to be back on.”
Finally, the end could be in sight.
Park Place Communities , a company based in Arizona, manages the mobile home community. Michael and Kayla Ayala are the owners and operators of the property.
Tenants received an email from the Arizona-based company on Nov. 1 saying the park will be coming under new ownership.
It read in part:
“We want to begin by apologizing for the recent challenges at our community in Alexandria. We truly appreciate your patience and understanding as we work through this period of transition. We’re pleased to share some exciting news — Park Place is now under contract with 3rd Son Property Group, who will be purchasing the property.”
Jordan Rahal, mobile homes Alexandria LLC lead partner, said he will be working alongside 3rd Son Property Group as they work through the sale and help tenants recover after a drawn-out period of uncertainty.
“Our model is to find parks that are having issues that aren’t performing to where they could be that need improvement that you know need love basically,” Rahal said.
Rahal said they’re working to get the water on as soon as possible, as early as the end of next week.
The city shut off the water to the park because, although people living there had been paying their landlord, the landlord hadn’t been paying the city. Alexandria Mayor Todd Naselroad said then that the landlord had racked up a bill of almost $100,000. He said the last time the account was paid in full was in February 2023. The last partial payment came through in January.
Naselroad said there were 13 attempts at a repayment agreement prior to the water being shut off. The current conditions at the mobile home park are at the heart of a class action lawsuit . It claims the mobile home has breached its contract with tenants and has caused intentional emotional distress, among other counts.
Rahal wouldn’t give all the details, but said that money will be paid to the city eventually, likely out of closing proceeds.
“Just out of respect to all parties involved, I’m not going to disclose too much there, but that will be resolved by the time we close,” Rahal said.
Many tenants thought they’d move away from the mobile home park before they ever saw running water in their homes again, but this news is keeping them in place for now.
“It means a lot to me, probably everybody else, that we have new owners,” Davis said. “I talk to them and I’m like, ‘I trust you guys.’ I don’t think it’s going to happen again.”
The email sent to tenants says both Park Place Communities and 3rd Son Property Group are hoping to finalize the sale within 60 days.
